analysis.summary: The coders split mainly because nothing says how to count entries. No rule says when one weapon or several guns make one entry, how loadout choices and passenger riders are listed, which weapon is the main one, or whether game-wide commands (retreat, reinforce, weapon pickup, Evacuate) are abilities at all. I propose plain counting rules for weapons: one in-game weapon is one entry; guns of the same family fired together are one entry; loadout variants that differ only in numbers are one entry; each passenger rider gets its own entry. I also propose a definition of the main weapon (what the buyer fires with primary fire, which for a loadout is the default choice), a shared-mechanics rule that keeps game-wide commands and universal keys off units, and fixed pattern lists for paired entries: a toggle and its alternate weapon both link the swap pattern and the effect pattern. Ability source becomes required, because one coder leaving out the default 'innate' caused all of the 63% score. The atypical lists need no rule of their own: they follow from the entry count and from the damage and family choices that other groups handle. Tie-breaks settle the repeated kind and source hesitations. Abilities with no fitting pattern are kept with a fit_note, coders never edit pattern files, and the RA3 samples need four small fixes to match the new rules.

proposals.evidence: Number of weapons: 61.1% agreement, all coders matched on only 3 of 6 units. Attack helicopter: A 8, B 6, C 7. A kept the Zuni rockets apart from the Hydra pods. proposals.root_cause: No rule says when two weapons are one entry. The Conventions count buttons ('anything fired with an attack button is a weapon'), and the only granularity text is 'one entry per distinct result' for passenger weapons. Nothing covers these cases: one weapon that acts differently by target; several guns fired together on one order (squads, twin guns); loadout choices that differ only in numbers; versions of a weapon across the titles of a series entry; weapons that come from game-wide orders.

proposals.change: New Conventions bullet: '- **Weapon entries.** Count weapon entries by these rules. (1) One in-game weapon is one entry, even when it acts differently against different targets. Code it as it works against its main target (the one its primary role is about, or else the one the source names first). List every target it can hit, and describe the other behaviour in the summary. (2) Weapons that the same seat fires together on one attack order are one entry when they share a family: twin guns, a squad's rifles plus its sergeant's carbine, a ground battery plus an air battery. Name them all and list every target any of them can hit. A weapon of another family fired with them is its own secondary entry. (3) Versions of one weapon across the titles of a series entry (the same place in the loadout, renamed or retuned) are one entry. Code the newest lead title's version and note the differences in the summary. (4) Loadout choices that differ only in numbers (damage, ammo, reload, blast size) are one entry; name them all. A choice that works differently (it homes, it is steered, it hits other targets) is its own entry. (5) A weapon whose kind depends on the donor is one adaptive entry. Do not list the donors. (6) Passenger weapons: one entry per rider unit (see when). Riders who fire their own guns from ports give no entries. (7) Never record an upgrade that only changes numbers, or a weapon the unit gets through a shared mechanic or a universal key (see Shared mechanics).' New unit.armament description, replacing 'Weapons, in slot order. Empty for unarmed units.': 'Weapons, main weapon first, counted by the Weapon entries rules in the Conventions. Empty for unarmed units.'

A drops the separate Zuni entry, B adds the Smart Rockets entry, C keeps the same count. Riflemen: 2 for all three. The tiers list names the universal keys (E pick up, G evict), but fields.md never says they are left off units. ability-sources has commander-power, but nothing says that a protocol touching every Soviet vehicle stays off each of them.

proposals.change: New Conventions bullet: '- **Shared mechanics and universal keys.** Some mechanics belong to the game, not the unit: every unit of its class has them, on its side or in the whole game. Examples are Company of Heroes infantry that retreat, reinforce, garrison, capture points, pick up dropped weapons and re-crew abandoned guns, and veterancy that every unit earns. Leave them off the unit's weapons and abilities. List each one once per game in that batch's registry note (research/registry-notes/games-r<batch>.md, section Game-wide mechanics), with the pattern it would link or the pattern wanted. If this unit does one of them better or worse than the rest (it captures faster), say so in its strengths or weaknesses. Do the same for actions that match one of our universal keys (enter or leave, pick up, shake off, bail out, switch seat, ping, evict passengers), even when the source gives the unit its own button for it, such as Evacuate. A side-wide power (a protocol, doctrine or general's power) that changes every unit of a class is left off too. A power that gives named unit types a new button is recorded on each of them, with source commander-power.'

proposals.side_effects: Cross-group (patterns): reinforce-squad, earn-veterancy and recover-wreck may end up with no source unit, because their main examples are game-wide. pattern.schema requires source_units with at least one entry, and the validator errors when no unit links a written pattern, so the patterns group should let game-level other_examples carry them. The missing retreat pattern stays a registry question. Scope: veterancy in RA2, RA3, Generals and CoH; garrison in RA2, RA3 and CoH; retreat and reinforce in CoH and Dawn of War; eject, seat switching and parachutes in Battlefield and PlanetSide 2; Iron Harvest weapon kits; RA3 protocols and Generals powers that touch whole classes. proposals.change: slot (whole text; the passenger and acquired parts come from passenger-entries and upgrade-weapons): 'primary = the main weapon: what the buyer fires with primary fire in the base form. Under decision 2A the buyer drives and fires it in a multi-seat unit, so its seat is driver. One per armed unit, listed first. For a loadout, the default choice is the primary. secondary = any other weapon the unit always has: on its own key, fired by another seat (a gunner's main gun is secondary), or of another family and fired with the primary. alternate = replaces the primary while an ability or mode is on; the primary is silent meanwhile. passenger = ... acquired = ... option = a loadout choice that is not fitted by default (see option_group).' option_group: old 'For option weapons: options in the same group exclude each other.' -> new 'Loadout group: every choice for one place in the loadout shares this id, and they exclude each other. The default choice keeps its primary or secondary slot; the other choices are option.' default: old 'For option weapons: the one fitted by default.' -> new 'true on the default choice of a loadout group, and nowhere else. A loadout place that starts empty has no default, and all its choices are option.' New Conventions bullet: '- **Main weapon.** A unit's main weapon is its one primary entry. The published samples link different lists on the two, which contradicts the convention. proposals.change: New bullet: '- **Paired entries.** Some weapons always come with an ability, and both entries of the pair link the same patterns. A weapon swapped in by an ability is an alternate weapon plus a toggle ability (deploy when the unit cannot move in one of the two states). Both link the swap pattern (switch-weapon-mode, or the mode's own pattern such as deploy-siege-mode) and the pattern of what the swapped-in weapon does, if one fits. A weapon gained on a kill is an acquired weapon plus a triggered ability, both linking the gain pattern (leech-weapon-on-kill). Passenger weapons come with one passive ability that links passenger-sets-weapon, as each passenger weapon does. The weapon used when nobody rides inside is a plain primary and links no passenger pattern.' Add to Granularity: 'A swapped-in weapon is still a weapon, so neither it nor its toggle links a pattern that mirrors its family or trait (a drain beam on a toggle links no drain-health). The mirroring patterns are mark-target, suppress-with-fire, leave-hazard-zone, drain-health, launch-drones, reveal-area and heal-self.'

verdicts.revised_change: New Conventions bullet: '- **Weapon entries.** Count weapon entries by these rules. (1) One in-game weapon is one entry, even when it acts differently against different targets. Code it as it works against its main target: the target its primary role is about, or else the one the source names first. List every target it can hit, and put the other behaviour in the summary. (2) Among the fixed weapons of one seat, make one entry per family. Copies of one gun are one entry (twin cannons, a squad's five rifles). So are different guns of one family that the seat uses on the same attack order, at once or each against its own kind of target (a sergeant's carbine with the squad's rifles, a ground battery with an air battery). Name them all and list every target any of them can hit. A gun of another family is its own entry. A gun of the same family on its own key or button (a pistol beside a rifle) is its own entry too. Where players set their own fire groups (MechWarrior), each family on a seat is one entry. (3) Rule 2 never merges a loadout choice, or a weapon the unit does not always have. Alternate, passenger, acquired and option weapons are counted by their own rules. (4) Versions of one weapon across the titles of a series entry (the same place in the loadout, renamed or retuned) are one entry. Code the version of the newest lead title that version_researched names (Battlefield 4), even when an older version works differently. Put the differences in the summary. (5) Loadout choices for one place are one entry when they would get the same family, damage, delivery, target list and traits. Name them all; range and other numbers may differ. Otherwise each choice is its own entry (Smart Rockets home, so they are apart). (6) A weapon whose kind depends on the donor is one adaptive acquired entry. Do not list the donors. Weapons gained in fixed steps (salvage crates) get one acquired entry per step that changes the family. (7) Passenger weapons follow the passenger slot rule. Riders who fire their own guns from ports give no entries. (8) Never record an upgrade that only changes numbers, or a weapon the unit gets through a shared mechanic or a universal key (see Shared mechanics).' verdicts.revised_change: New Conventions bullet: '- **Shared mechanics and universal keys.** Some mechanics belong to the game, not the unit: every unit of its class has them, on its side or in the whole game, apart from a few named exceptions. Examples are basic orders (move, attack, stop, hold, patrol, stances), Company of Heroes infantry that retreat, reinforce, garrison, capture points, pick up dropped weapons and re-crew abandoned guns, and veterancy that every unit earns. If this unit does a listed mechanic better or worse than the rest (it captures faster), say so in its strengths or weaknesses. Leave off actions that match one of our universal keys (enter or leave, pick up, shake off, bail out, switch seat, ping, evict passengers), even when the source gives the unit its own button for it, such as Evacuate.
